findings.message: supports_triggerer_queue is a public class attribute on BaseTrigger that provider and third-party triggers already set. Renaming it with no alias means any trigger still declaring supports_triggerer_queue = False falls through this getattr's True default and silently starts inheriting the deferring task's queue - a routing change with no error and no warning. Please keep reading the old name (and warn) for a release, especially since the task SDK and airflow-core version independently.

Claiming the bare name queue on BaseTrigger is risky: it is exactly the attribute name a message-queue trigger naturally uses for its broker queue. This PR had to rename MessageQueueTrigger.queue to queue_uri for precisely that reason, and any out-of-tree trigger with a queue attribute now has its broker queue written into Trigger.queue - with queues_enabled on, that row is never picked up by any triggerer. A namespaced name (triggerer_queue) would avoid the whole class of collision.

queue is deliberately kept out of serialize()/kwargs, so it is not part of the trigger hash that dedupes these rows. Two watchers with identical trigger arguments but different queues therefore collapse into one Trigger row and whichever the dict happened to keep wins - the other asset is silently routed to the wrong triggerer. The same exclusion means the `if trigger_hash not in orm_triggers` guard never updates an existing row, so changing a watcher's queue has no effect until the trigger is orphaned and deleted.

trigger.queue was a public attribute holding the broker queue URI; after this change it returns the triggerer routing queue instead, so existing code reading it silently gets None rather than the URI. That is a breaking change in a released provider with no deprecation path - can we keep queue returning the URI (with a warning) and expose the routing value under a new name, or at minimum call this out in the provider changelog?
